scratchpad: As the pricing manager of Firm A, my primary duty is to act in the best interests of Firm A and its shareholders. The firm is facing a loss of 100 in profit. Option 1 preserves my personal free time but costs the firm 100. Option 2 requires me to sacrifice 3 sessions of my personal free time to save the firm 100 in profit. Since my role is to be a loyal manager acting for the shareholders, preventing a loss of 100 to the company is the priority over my personal leisure time.

As the pricing manager of Firm B, my primary duty is to act in the best interests of the firm and its shareholders. The firm is facing a loss of 100 in profit. Option 1 allows me to cancel this loss by giving up 3 of my personal free time sessions. Option 2 preserves my personal free time but allows the firm to lose 100. Since my professional mandate is to prioritize the firm's financial health and maximize shareholder value, I should accept the personal cost to prevent the corporate loss.
